MeterRemaining.description: Free metered GET requests left today for this IP (see the metering note in the API description).

MeterReset.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) at which this IP's free daily metered-GET quota resets: the next 00:00 UTC. Same shape as X-RateLimit-Reset. Lets a caller behind a shared egress IP tell when the per-IP quota rolls over.

AggregateStats.description: Aggregate statistics about the x402 ecosystem

avg_uptime_method.description: How per-network avg_uptime is computed. Identical to the method used by /networks.

computed_at.description: When this response was generated (ISO 8601, UTC). The precomputed traction figures carry their own traction.as_of, which can be older.

facilitator_volume_note.description: In-band note framing facilitator_volume_usd_30d as a non-deduped superset of the listed-services flow

facilitator_volume_usd_30d.description: TRENO A D9: aggregate settlement volume (USD) across measured (enabled) facilitators, summed from daily snapshots whose UTC day starts within the last 30 days (the last 29 full UTC days plus today so far). A non-deduped SUPERSET of the listed-services flow (it is not restricted to listed payTo mappings), so it is not comparable one-to-one with the traction block. null (never a fabricated 0) until facilitator snapshots exist. See facilitator_volume_note.

listing_growth.description: TRENO A D9: how many services were first listed recently.

new_30d.description: Services first listed in the last 30 days

new_7d.description: Services first listed in the last 7 days

networks.description: Per-network breakdown over the same networks total_networks counts, testnets included and flagged by is_mainnet. Ordered by service_count, descending.

abbreviation.description: Network label: the abbreviation served by /networks when the network is in that list (e.g. BSE, SOL), otherwise the chain name (e.g. Ethereum), or the lowercased network id for a chain not yet identified (e.g. animica:1).

on_chain_measurement.description: Where on-chain settlement measurement starts. Settlements are harvested from a floor date and networks came online on different dates, so an aggregate over a window that starts before all_networks_measured_since does not cover every network.

all_networks_measured_since.description: The day from which every measured network contributes (ISO 8601, UTC midnight). null before the first daily facilitator snapshot exists.

measured_since.description: Earliest measured day across networks (ISO 8601, UTC midnight). null before the first daily facilitator snapshot exists.

note.description: Fixed in-band note restating the meaning of the two dates

payment_ready_count.description: Number of services in the BASE payment-ready tier (treno D3): answered a valid x402 challenge and alive within the decay window (a probe success within the last 7 days, or api-key exempt). Same predicate as the ?payment_ready=true list filter. The broad signal verified_count used to carry.

total_networks.description: Count of distinct mainnet networks that carry current pricing on an active endpoint of a listed service, recomputed live from the pricing rows. Every raw network spelling is resolved to one chain identity, so several spellings of one chain count once; testnets and spellings known to be invalid are excluded, and a chain not yet in the identity registry still counts. networks[] is built on the same set, so total_networks equals the number of networks[] entries with is_mainnet true.

total_networks_note.description: Human-readable reminder of the total_networks semantics served in-band with the response

traction.description: Measured on-chain traction aggregated across ALL listed services over a window that starts at 00:00 UTC 30 days back, so 30 full UTC days plus today so far. This is not the same window as the per-service assessment.traction figures, which use a rolling 30 days ending when each snapshot was computed. Computed directly over the raw settlements, deduplicated on settlement identity (network, tx_hash, log_index), and NEVER summed from the per-service assessment.traction figures (distinct buyers are not additive across services, and summing pro-quota volume would reintroduce shared-attribution rounding). USDC only, via measured facilitators: a measured floor across the listed directory, not an ecosystem total.

as_of.description: When the precomputed coverage and concentration figures (coverage_of_measured_flow_pct, top_10_services_share_pct, top_1_service_*) were last computed (ISO 8601, UTC). They refresh hourly and can lag the totals above. null before the first precompute.

caveat.description: In-band honesty note: a measured floor across listed services over 30d, not an ecosystem total; USDC via measured facilitators only

coverage_of_measured_flow_pct.description: Coverage KPI: the listed dedup settlement volume (volume_usd_30d) as a percentage of the flow measurable by our tracked settlers over the same UTC-day-anchored window (the facilitator daily volume we measure, NOT the whole ecosystem, so it is a floor on our coverage of the flow we can see). Precomputed hourly; null until the first refresh (never a fake 0). The denominator is also declared in-band in method.

measured_flow_freshness.description: How fresh the flow behind coverage_of_measured_flow_pct is (W2-13#3). Coverage says how much of the measurable flow we cover, not whether that flow is still being ingested: a settler-sync cursor frozen hours ago keeps serving a coverage figure that looks current. Measured at SYNC-GROUP grain (facilitator x network x token), which is the unit that actually freezes: a facilitator can sync Base every 15 minutes while its Solana groups have not completed in hours, and rolling that up by newest completion would report it as live. Always present as a key; null only when the freshness read itself failed at response time (the rest of the response still serves). An empty sync state is never null: it reads 0 of 0, never a fabricated freshness. Aggregate only, and it reports the same sync-state table, at the same grain and with the same 2-hour threshold, as the ingest block of GET /api/health, which is where the site-level liveness verdict lives.

oldest_cursor_age_seconds.description: Age, in whole seconds at response time, of the most-behind sync GROUP's last clean settler-sync completion (not the most-behind facilitator: a partly frozen facilitator is reported by its frozen group, never by its freshest one). null when no tracked group has ever completed a sync (an absence of measurement, never a fresh 0); such a group is counted in stale_sync_groups.

stale_facilitators.description: Facilitators with AT LEAST ONE frozen sync group. Any-stale on purpose: a facilitator counts here as soon as part of its ingest is frozen, even while its other networks keep completing, because the flow it contributes is already partial. Read it next to stale_sync_groups: how many settlement paths are affected, against how much of the ingest.

stale_sync_groups.description: Sync groups whose cursor is frozen past the staleness threshold (2 hours, well above the 15-minute sync cadence) or that never completed a sync. This is the size of the freeze: the settlement flow those groups carry is decaying, so a non-zero value means the coverage figure is computed over a partly stale window.

total_facilitators.description: Facilitators carrying a settler-sync state row at all: the denominator for stale_facilitators.

total_sync_groups.description: Settler-sync groups (facilitator x network x token) tracked at all: the denominator for stale_sync_groups.

measured_networks.description: Network abbreviations settled on in the window (e.g. BSE, SOL). Abbreviations here, unlike the per-service traction block which uses CAIP-2 ids. Empty until the first hourly precompute.

measured_services.description: Number of listed services with at least one attributed settlement in the window (walks the payTo mapping with the last_seen + 1 day grace). null until the first hourly precompute, never a fake 0.

method.description: How the aggregate is computed: dedup on settlement identity, never a sum of the per-service figures; also declares the coverage_of_measured_flow_pct denominator and the top_10_services_share_pct basis in-band

settlement_count_30d.description: Deduped settlement count across listed services over the window above. Distinct from any per-service tx_count_30d: this is a count of deduped settlement legs, not a sum. null until the first hourly precompute, never a fake 0.

top_10_services_share_pct.description: Concentration disclosure: the share of the 30d dedup volume held by the top 10 services (ranked by volume via the payTo mapping). The numerator is the deduped settlements mapped to any top-10 service, never a sum of the per-service figures; the denominator is the same whole-window dedup total (volume_usd_30d). Precomputed hourly; null until the first refresh.

top_1_service_imported.description: Whether that single largest service is an auto-imported listing (its source starts with imported) rather than an operator submission, so the concentration is not read as operator traction. null until the first refresh, or when the service cannot be resolved (never a guessed flag).

top_1_service_share_pct.description: Concentration disclosure one level deeper than top_10: the share of the 30d dedup volume held by the SINGLE largest service (ranked by volume via the payTo mapping). By construction top_1 <= top_10. Same hourly precompute; null until the first refresh (never a fake 0).

top_1_service_top_buyer_share_pct.description: One level deeper again: within that single largest service, the share of ITS 30d volume held by its own single largest buyer. Same hourly precompute; null until the first refresh (never a fake 0).

unique_buyers_30d.description: Distinct on-chain buyer addresses across listed services over the window above (deduplicated, not a sum of per-service buyer counts). null until the first hourly precompute commits the cache row, never a fake 0.

volume_usd_30d.description: USDC settlement volume across listed services over the window above (USD; a measured floor, not summed from per-service figures). null until the first hourly precompute, never a fake 0.

verified_count.description: Number of services in the FORTE verified tier (treno D3): a paid delivery-probe settled and delivered, drift-revocable. Same predicate as the ?verified=true list filter. Starts at 0 and grows only with real payments. SEMANTIC CHANGE: this used to count the broad "answers a valid 402 and is alive" set, which is now payment_ready_count.

AiMarkedField.description: An AI-derived (assessment family 10) field with its own provenance. value may be "unknown" when the model could not ground it in the measured signals. Never overrides a measured value.

value.description: The AI-derived value (string or array of strings), or "unknown"

AssessAnswer.description: The AI-marked recommendation over the shortlist (family 10 advisor). AI-derived; not an endorsement, and it never overrides a measured value.

ranking.description: Candidates ordered best-first for the need; only slugs from the request appear (the model can never introduce one).

confidence.description: 0-1: how strongly the signals support the recommendation

value.description: One plain-language paragraph answering the need

AssessReport.description: The modular assessment report body: one block per priced module. It always carries the advisor answer under answer; a probe_report block is added when a live probe ran. Future modules add their own block additively.

probe_report.description: Present only when a live probe ran (the request carried a probe target and live probing was armed). The truncated probe result; never the verbatim third-party body.

AssessRequest.description: On-demand assessment request: a need plus the shortlist of service slugs to compare for it.

probe.description: Optional live-probe target: also pay one listed service for real and analyze what it returns. When live probing is armed the single accepts[0] amount becomes $0.25 plus that endpoint price X, and the report gains a probe_report block; probe fees are non-refundable regardless of outcome. Ignored (advisor-only) when live probing is not armed.

endpoint_path.description: Optional URL path on that service to probe, beginning with '/'. Omit to let the server pick the cheapest priced USDC-on-Base endpoint. Templated paths (with {param} or :param placeholders) cannot be probed live and are excluded from probing.

slug.description: Slug of one listed service to probe live.

question.description: The need to assess the shortlist against (1 to 1000 characters).

services.description: Service slugs to compare (1 to 8, de-duplicated, order kept).

Assessment.description: Full evidence-backed per-service assessment. Measured families are read-only plain values; the synthesis block is AI-derived and marked. "unknown"/null are honest, not zero.

compliance.description: Family 2: x402 conformance grade + per-check ok/x list (14 checks, of which three cover signability: the declared x402 version, the EIP-712 domain parameters on every EVM entry, and whether a v2 envelope travelled in the payment-required header), payTo source/location (deterministic). Each check is true, false, or null when it could not be evaluated, and a null never counts as a failure

domain.description: Family 4: domain age, registrar, free-host flag (measured)

economics.description: Family 5 (measured): entry price (min USD + atomic) and its in-category percentile, plus the full price picture for tiered services: price_max_usd (highest tier), category_percentile_max, endpoint_count, distinct_price_count, pricing model and stability

input_hash.description: Hash of the normalized inputs the assessment was computed over

model_id.description: LLM model id used for the synthesis block (null when no synthesis ran)

reliability.description: Family 1: uptime windows, p95/avg response, freshness, failures, total checks (measured)

risk.description: Family 8: deterministic risk level + flags (blocklist/impersonation only; never AI, never from low uptime or high price)

synthesis.description: Family 10: AI-derived summary/capability_tags/category/inputs/outputs/auth, each an AiMarkedField {value,confidence,source:"ai"}; never overrides a measured value

traction.description: Family 6: measured on-chain settlement traction (volume/buyers/concentration over the payTo mapping, USDC, a conservative undercount); null on rows assessed before this field existed

AssessmentSummary.description: Compact per-service assessment summary carried on each list item (backs relevance/quality ranking). Measured sub-scores are plain; capability_tags/summary are AI-derived and marked.

capability_tags.description: AI-derived capability tags, marked {value,confidence,source:"ai"}; null when the model could not ground them

category_percentile.description: 0-100 within its category, ranked on the min price (lower = cheaper)

category_percentile_max.description: 0-100, ranked on the max price among every service max price in the category

compliance_failed_checks.description: Machine-stable ids of the conformance checks that failed (pass=false); [] = all pass, null = no compliance graded. Human labels are in the detail assessment.compliance.checks[]. The three signability ids are eip712_domain_extra (at least one EVM route carries no EIP-712 domain parameters, so a standard x402 client cannot sign a payment for it), x402_version_current (a captured payload declares an x402 version other than the current 2) and version_channel_coherent (an envelope declaring x402 version 2 was delivered only in the response body, not in the payment-required header). Only eip712_domain_extra caps the grade; the other two are facts about the envelope that do not stop a payment from being signed

compliance_grade.description: x402 conformance grade over the deterministic checklist (the share of evaluable checks the service passes). One ceiling applies: a service with at least one EVM route missing the EIP-712 domain parameters a standard x402 client needs in order to sign (check eip712_domain_extra = false) does not grade above C, however clean the rest of the envelope is. "unknown" means nothing has been observed yet, which is not a failure.

compliance_passed.description: How many of the evaluable checks passed

compliance_total.description: How many checks could be evaluated at all: the denominator of the grade, up to 14. It is lower when a check does not apply (a Solana-only service has no EVM entry for the EIP-712 domain check) or could not be observed; a not-evaluable check is never counted as a failure

distinct_price_count.description: Count of distinct current prices (1 = flat, >1 = tiered)

price_max_usd.description: Decimal USD (highest tier); equals price_usd when flat. null on rows assessed before this field existed

reliability_uptime_30d.description: Measured 30d uptime percentage; null = not yet measured

summary.description: AI-derived one-line summary, marked {value,confidence,source:"ai"}; null when unknown

traction.description: Family 6 measured on-chain traction (same block as the detail); null on rows assessed before this field existed

BestRecommendation.description: One ranked service recommendation from GET /best. All *_usd fields are decimal US dollars.

capability_tags.description: AI-derived capability tags marked {value, confidence, source:"ai"}, or null when the model could not ground them

compliance_failed_checks.description: Ids of the conformance checks that failed; [] = all pass, null = none graded. eip712_domain_extra here means a standard x402 client cannot sign a payment for at least one route of this service

compliance_grade.description: x402 conformance grade, capped at C when at least one EVM route is missing the EIP-712 domain parameters a standard x402 client needs in order to sign

payment_ready.description: BASE tier (treno D3): answers a valid x402 challenge and is alive. The broad signal verified used to carry.

price_max_usd.description: Highest tier price in USD; equals min_price_usd when flat

relevance.description: Relevance sub-score (0-1) when a free-text q was given, else null

score.description: Final blended score (0-1), rounded to 2 decimals

top_buyer_share_30d.description: 0-1 concentration of the single largest buyer over the same rolling 30-day window. Also scored: it discounts the traction term, by up to half when a single buyer accounts for all of the volume

verified.description: FORTE tier (treno D3): paid delivery-probe settled and delivered, drift-revocable, no time decay. The tier require_verified filters on.

volume_usd_30d.description: Settlement volume in USD over a rolling 30-day window ending when the traction snapshot was computed (not aligned to UTC days). Conservative undercount; pro-quota on a shared payout

BestResult.description: The GET /best data block: ranked recommendations plus the ranking basis, danger-excluded slugs, and optional facilitator context.

excluded_danger.description: Slugs removed from the recommendation set by a deterministic danger flag (blocklist or impersonation match only).

facilitator_context.description: Top facilitators by 7d settlement volume when include_facilitator_context=true, otherwise null.

note.description: Present only when no service matched the given filters.

ranking_basis.description: Plain-language description of how the ranking was produced (the two-stage relevance-then-quality blend).

BuyersPoint.description: One UTC-day bucket of the distinct on-chain buyers a service settled with (counted from the raw settlements, not summed from a rollup)

unique_buyers.description: Distinct buyer addresses observed settling that day

CanonicalAccept.description: One canonical accepts[] entry captured from the live 402 wire, tied to the endpoint it was observed on. Field names are the stored snapshot shape (camelCase), passed through verbatim.

payTo.description: Receiving wallet address, verbatim (Solana base58 is case-significant, never lowercased)

ChangeSummary.description: Precomputed diff for the event. Fields are populated per event type: payto_changed carries the payTo deltas, price_changed carries priceChanges, schema_changed carries the schema/endpoint deltas. An absent field means no change of that kind.

newPrice.description: Comma-joined distinct new prices under the same key

oldPrice.description: Comma-joined distinct old prices under this endpoint/scheme/network/asset key

FacilitatorBuyers.description: Per-chain distinct on-chain buyers (E3). total_upper_bound_30d is a declared UPPER BOUND: buyers on different chains or tokens are not de-duplicated, and each per-chain figure sums daily distinct counts. Prefer the per-chain figures.

network_caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifier; null when the raw chain id is not recognized

unique_buyers_30d.description: Distinct buyers on this chain over the trailing 30 days (sum of daily distinct counts)

caveat.description: Mandatory in-band note declaring why the total is an upper bound

total_upper_bound_30d.description: Straight sum of the per-chain figures: a strict upper bound, not an exact head count

FacilitatorChainBreakdown.description: A facilitator volume on one (network, token). "on-chain" rows carry measured volume; "listed" rows are declared-but-not-yet-measured chains.

last_activity_at.description: Most recent on-chain settlement activity on this chain

network.description: Chain identifier as configured ('base', full-length 'solana:5eykt…' genesis hash, or CAIP-2 eip155:*); kept raw for backwards compatibility. Prefer network_caip2 for joins.

network_caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifier for cross-endpoint joins (matches /networks .caip2 and service pricing .network_caip2); null when the raw chain identifier is not recognized

token_address.description: Settlement token contract/mint address on that chain

token_address_norm.description: Normalized settlement token address for cross-endpoint joins: EVM addresses lowercased, non-EVM (e.g. Solana mints) kept as-is; null = unknown

tx_count_all.description: Settlement transaction count over all recorded history

verification.description: "on-chain" if measured volume > 0 on this chain, else "listed"

volume_usd_24h.description: On-chain volume for today (UTC) so far, not a trailing 24-hour window: it resets at 00:00 UTC (USD)

volume_usd_30d.description: On-chain volume over the trailing 30 days (USD)

volume_usd_7d.description: On-chain volume over the trailing 7 days (USD)

volume_usd_all.description: On-chain volume over all recorded history (USD)

FacilitatorContext.description: Ecosystem facilitator context (NOT per-service): top facilitators by 7d settlement volume with a two-state verification flag.

verification.description: "on-chain" iff observed on-chain volume greater than zero, else "listed"

FacilitatorDetail.description: Full detail for a single facilitator (TRENO A D5). Carries the list-row fields plus avg $/settlement, a 7d-vs-previous-7d trend, per-chain buyers (an upper bound), the per-(network,token) chains breakdown with first_activity_at, the on-chain settlers, the daily series (honoring period=all), and the listed_services bridge.

avg_settlement_usd_30d.description: Average USD per settlement over the trailing 30 days; null when there are no settlements.

avg_settlement_usd_all.description: Average USD per settlement over all history (volume_usd_all / tx_count_all); null when tx_count_all is 0 (never a fabricated 0).

caveat.description: In-band caveat: a measured floor, the avg/trend semantics, and the 24h today-so-far note.

method.description: In-band method frame: volume measured directly on-chain by settler-address attribution (USDC), never self-reported.

series.description: Daily volume series (oldest first). With series_by=total each point is { date, volume_usd, tx_count }; with series_by=chain each point is { date, network, volume_usd }.

settler_count.description: Number of enabled on-chain settler addresses (EOAs)

trend_7d_vs_prev_7d.description: Ratio of the last 7 days' volume to the previous 7 days' (same-length windows, so it IS the daily-rate comparison); null when the previous window is empty. Invariant, never re-divided.

tx_count_24h.description: Settlement count for today (UTC) so far

volume_usd_24h.description: On-chain USDC volume for today (UTC) so far, not a trailing 24-hour window (USD)

volume_usd_30d.description: On-chain USDC volume over the trailing 30 days (USD)

volume_usd_7d.description: On-chain USDC volume over the trailing 7 days (USD)

volume_usd_all.description: On-chain USDC volume over all recorded history (USD)

FacilitatorDetailChain.description: A facilitator volume on one (network, token), as served on the detail node. Same shape as FacilitatorChainBreakdown plus first_activity_at (C3).

first_activity_at.description: First on-chain settlement activity on this chain (C3); null when never seen

last_activity_at.description: Most recent on-chain settlement activity on this chain

network.description: Chain identifier as configured ('base', full Solana genesis hash, or eip155:*); prefer network_caip2 for joins.

network_caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifier; null when the raw chain id is not recognized

token_address.description: Settlement token contract/mint address on that chain

token_address_norm.description: Normalized settlement token address (EVM lowercased, non-EVM kept as-is); null = unknown

tx_count_all.description: Settlement count over all recorded history

verification.description: "on-chain" if measured volume > 0 on this chain, else "listed"

volume_usd_24h.description: On-chain volume for today (UTC) so far (USD)

volume_usd_30d.description: On-chain volume over the trailing 30 days (USD)

volume_usd_7d.description: On-chain volume over the trailing 7 days (USD)

volume_usd_all.description: On-chain volume over all recorded history (USD)

FacilitatorListItem.description: A facilitator with independently on-chain-verified USDC volume across all measured chains. For USDC, USD volume equals token volume 1:1.

chains.description: Per-(network,token) volume breakdown; present only when include=chains

first_activity_at.description: Earliest measured settlement day (start of our measurement window, not the facilitator first on-chain activity, which can predate it by months); extends back as history is backfilled. null when never measured. Use it to tell a facilitator whose all-time spans its whole life from one whose window is only weeks deep.

settler_count.description: Number of enabled on-chain settler addresses (EOAs)

timeseries.description: Daily volume series (oldest first); present only when include=timeseries

tx_count_24h.description: Settlement transaction count for today (UTC) so far, not a trailing 24-hour window: it resets at 00:00 UTC

tx_count_30d.description: Settlement transaction count over the trailing 30 days

tx_count_7d.description: Settlement transaction count over the trailing 7 days

tx_count_all.description: Settlement transaction count over all recorded history (from Jan 2026 when the history backfill is enabled)

verification.description: "on-chain" when settlement volume has been measured directly from blockchain transactions (volume_usd_all > 0); "listed" when the facilitator is catalogued but no volume has been measured yet

volume_usd_24h.description: On-chain USDC volume for today (UTC) so far, not a trailing 24-hour window: it resets at 00:00 UTC (USD)

volume_usd_30d.description: On-chain USDC volume over the trailing 30 days (USD)

volume_usd_7d.description: On-chain USDC volume over the trailing 7 days (USD)

volume_usd_all.description: On-chain USDC volume over all recorded history (USD; from Jan 2026 when the history backfill is enabled)

FacilitatorListedServices.description: The facilitator -> listed-services bridge (D2 + C1): which directory services have settled on-chain via this facilitator. Volume is the service 30d figure over its payout mapping (a conservative floor); a service sharing a payout address is counted at the address level here (not re-divided pro-quota, since the split is per-service, not per-facilitator).

active_count_30d.description: Listed services with an attributed settlement via this facilitator over the trailing 30 days

all_time_count.description: Distinct listed services that settled via this facilitator over all history; null until the hourly precompute records it (never a fabricated 0).

caveat.description: In-band note: shared/address-level attribution and the null all-time-count until precompute

top.description: Top listed services by 30d volume (up to 10), link-able by slug

volume_usd_30d.description: Service 30d settlement volume over its payout mapping (USD)

timeframe.description: Window used to sort the results

FacilitatorSettler.description: An enabled on-chain settler address (EOA) for this facilitator.

enabled.description: Whether the settler is currently enabled for measurement

last_seen_at.description: Most recent time this settler was observed settling

network_caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifier; null when the raw chain id is not recognized

source.description: How the settler address was discovered (e.g. x402scan, submitted)

token_name.description: Settlement token label on this chain (e.g. USDC)

FacilitatorSubmissionRequest.description: Facilitator submission body, selected by "type": "facilitator". Facilitators are settlement infrastructure: they are verified by on-chain settlement activity from their settler addresses, never by an HTTP 402 probe. Approved facilitators are listed on GET /facilitators with verification "listed" and switch to "on-chain" automatically once settlement volume is measured.

claimed_volume_usd.description: Optional self-reported all-time settlement volume in USD (informational only; cross-checked against the on-chain probe at review)

description.description: Optional description of what the facilitator does

facilitator_id_slug.description: Optional proposed identifier slug (lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens). Reserved names are flagged for manual review.

networks.description: Declared settlement networks (e.g. "base", "polygon", "solana"). Enabled EVM chains are probed on-chain before review; other chains are recorded as declared claims. Also accepted as one comma/newline separated string.

settler_addresses.description: On-chain addresses that originate settlement transactions: 0x EVM addresses (40 hex chars) or base58 Solana addresses (32-44 chars). Also accepted as one comma/newline separated string.

token_claims.description: Optional list of tokens the facilitator claims to settle (informational only)

type.description: Selects the facilitator branch of POST /submit

website_url.description: Public website URL (own domain; free hosting and dev-tunnel domains are rejected)

FacilitatorTimeseriesPoint.description: One day of a facilitator on-chain volume series

GlobalCheckEntry.description: A check entry with service info, for the global live feed

Network.description: A blockchain network that x402 services accept payments on

avg_uptime.description: Per-service mean of the latest daily uptime rollup for services on this network (see meta.avg_uptime_method)

caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifier for cross-endpoint joins (exact casing, Solana reference truncated to 32 chars). Matches network_caip2 in service pricing and facilitator chains. Falls back to caip2_id for networks not yet in the canonical map.

caip2_id.description: CAIP-2 chain identifier as stored (may be lowercase, e.g. the Solana reference); kept for backwards compatibility. Prefer caip2 for joins.

service_count.description: Number of services accepting payments on this network

PaymentRequired.description: x402 v2 PaymentRequired body returned on a 402 (also base64-encoded in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED response header).

message.description: Human-readable explanation with a pointer to /api (body only; absent from the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header)

resource.description: The paid resource this 402 guards (echoed by the x402 server).

description.example: Resubmission fee after a rejected submission

PaymentRequirements.description: A single x402 payment option (one element of accepts[]).

amount.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals) as a string; "500000" = $0.50

PricePoint.description: One captured 402 price observation for a service, at one endpoint/network/asset

network.description: Network id the price was recorded on

PricingEntry.description: Current pricing for an endpoint on a specific network

asset_address.description: Token contract/mint address as reported by the service (casing may vary); null = unknown/not reported

asset_address_norm.description: Normalized token address for cross-endpoint joins: EVM addresses lowercased, non-EVM (e.g. Solana mints) kept as-is; null = unknown/not reported

network.description: Network ID as reported by the service (usually CAIP-2, casing may vary); kept raw for backwards compatibility. Prefer network_caip2 for joins.

network_caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifier for cross-endpoint joins (matches /networks .caip2 and facilitator chains .network_caip2); null when the raw network id is not recognized

price_usd.description: Price in USD; null when the asset is not USD-priceable (a non-canonical token we do not value in USD)

ProbeReport.description: Live-probe result block (treno 4). The report of a real x402 payment to one listed service and an analysis of what it returned. It carries a verdict plus truncated evidence snippets and NEVER the verbatim third-party body. All *_atomic fields are atomic USDC (6-decimal integer strings), not dollars. Probe fees are non-refundable regardless of outcome.

ai_analysis.description: AI verdict on what the endpoint returned, marked {value, confidence, source:'ai'}; null when the model missed or the key is unset. Fail-soft, and it never contains the verbatim body.

extracts.description: Up to 3 truncated evidence snippets (each hard-capped); NEVER the verbatim third-party body.

http_status.description: Endpoint HTTP status after payment, or null.

live_price_atomic.description: Live endpoint price observed on the fresh 402 (atomic USDC string), or null when unreadable.

note.description: Policy note: charged $0.25 plus X, non-refundable regardless of outcome, snippets truncated, full response never resold.

outcome.description: settled = paid and analyzed; price_drift = the live price moved above the quote, so nothing was paid; endpoint_error = paid but the endpoint failed or was unreadable.

paid_atomic.description: Atomic USDC actually sent to the endpoint ('0' when nothing was spent, e.g. on price_drift).

quoted_x_atomic.description: Endpoint price X quoted at assessment time (atomic USDC string).

schema_conformance.description: Deterministic verdict on the returned body from its declared content type and parseability.

settle_ok.description: true only when the OUTBOUND probe payment settled on-chain (a tx_hash is present).

network.description: Canonical CAIP-2 network of the probed endpoint.

tx_hash.description: On-chain settlement tx hash of the outbound probe payment, or null when nothing settled.

version.description: probe_report block generation; bumps when this block shape changes.

Provenance.description: Data provenance and license block. Present once per response, top-level in the envelope alongside data (and meta where present), never per item. Declares the CC BY 4.0 data license and how to attribute this data.

attribution.description: Ready-to-use attribution string to display when reusing this data.

attribution_required.description: Whether attribution is required when reusing this data (always true under CC BY 4.0).

cite_as.description: Canonical URL to cite as the source of this specific resource: the human-readable page where one exists, otherwise the request URL without its query string.

license.description: SPDX identifier of the data license (Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International).

source.description: Canonical site origin behind the directory.

ScorePoint.description: One assessment run projected to its measured sub-scores (the sub-scores only: no ranked composite score, no AI-derived fields)

compliance_total.description: Checks evaluable at that run: the denominator AS MEASURED then, which is why it must be read per point. It moved from 11 to 14 when the signability checks landed, and older points are left as they were recorded

ServiceChangeEvent.description: A change detected on a service live 402 wire, joined to the service it belongs to.

old_snapshot.description: Canonical accepts[] before the change; null on a first observation.

type.description: What moved: payTo (settlement address) rotation, price move, or schema change.

ServiceDetail.description: Full service detail including endpoints with pricing

assessment.description: Full evidence-backed per-service assessment (T1, free): reliability, x402 compliance, site/docs reachability, domain/identity, economics, deterministic risk, plus an AI synthesis. null until the service is first assessed. Measured families are read-only plain values; synthesis fields are AI-derived and marked {value,confidence,source:"ai"}, and a computed value never overrides a measured one.

consecutive_failures.description: Number of consecutive failed checks; 0 when the service is stable. Internal negative monitor sentinels are clamped to 0.

last_success_at.description: Most recent time the monitor observed a successful 402 probe; null when never observed up.

min_price_usd.description: Lowest price in USD across all endpoints

networks.description: Network abbreviations aggregated across all active endpoints

networks_caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifiers for cross-endpoint joins, index-aligned with networks. Falls back to the stored network id for networks not yet in the canonical map, mirroring /networks .caip2

payment_ready.description: BASE tier (treno D3): the endpoint answered a valid x402 402 challenge and is alive within the decay window (a probe success within the last 7 days, or api-key exempt). Ages back to false past the window and heals on the next good probe; the historical fact is never erased. This is the broad discovery signal verified used to carry.

payment_ready_until.description: When the payment-ready tier decays if no further successful probe lands (last_success_at + 7 days); null when the service was never observed up.

source.description: Provenance (D4): how this listing entered the directory. "submitted" = an operator or user submitted it through /submit; "imported:<origin>" = auto-imported from a public x402 index (not an operator endorsement). An operator can claim and correct an imported listing through the owner-update flow at /services/{slug}/update.

uptime.description: Uptime percentage per trailing window; each window is null when the service has not been monitored yet (null = not yet monitored, 0 = observed down)

uptime_24h.description: Uptime percentage over last 24 hours; null = not yet monitored (no checks recorded in the window)

verified.description: FORTE tier (treno D3): a paid delivery-probe settled on-chain and delivered AND the badge was not since revoked on payTo/schema drift. It has NO time-based decay - it decays one-way through the monitor drift hook and re-earns only by paying again. SEMANTIC CHANGE: this field previously carried the broad "answers a valid 402 and is alive" signal, which is now payment_ready. Starts empty and grows only with real payments, so it can be false for a service that is very much alive.

verified_until.description: Always null: the FORTE verified tier has no time-based expiry (it decays on payTo/schema drift, not on a timer). Read payment_ready_until for the payment-ready decay clock. Retained for shape stability.

ServiceListItem.description: A service in the directory listing with computed summary fields

assessment.description: Compact per-service assessment summary (evidence-backed). null until the service is first assessed. Measured sub-scores are plain values; capability_tags and summary are AI-derived and carry {value,confidence,source:"ai"} provenance so an AI guess is never mistaken for a measured fact.

min_price_usd.description: Lowest price in USD across all endpoints

networks.description: Network abbreviations supported by this service (e.g. ["BSE", "SOL"])

networks_caip2.description: Canonical CAIP-2 identifiers for cross-endpoint joins, index-aligned with networks (e.g. ["eip155:8453", "solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp"]). Falls back to the stored network id for networks not yet in the canonical map, mirroring /networks .caip2, so service-to-network joins never silently break

payment_ready.description: BASE tier (treno D3): the endpoint answered a valid x402 402 challenge and is alive within the decay window (a probe success within the last 7 days, or api-key exempt). The broad discovery signal the verified field used to carry.

source.description: Provenance (D4): how this listing entered the directory. "submitted" = an operator or user submitted it through /submit; "imported:<origin>" = auto-imported from a public x402 index (not an operator endorsement). An operator can claim and correct an imported listing through the owner-update flow at /services/{slug}/update.

uptime_24h.description: Uptime percentage over last 24 hours; null = not yet monitored (no checks recorded in the window)

verified.description: FORTE tier (treno D3): a paid delivery-probe settled on-chain and delivered AND the badge was not since revoked on payTo/schema drift. No time decay. SEMANTIC CHANGE: this field previously carried the broad "answers a valid 402 and is alive" signal, which is now payment_ready.

ServiceSubmissionRequest.description: Service submission body: the default branch of POST /submit when "type" is omitted

category.description: Service category (use /categories to get valid values)

description.description: Brief description of what the service does

endpoints.description: List of endpoint paths to probe (e.g. ["/v1/generate", "/v1/translate"])

type.description: Optional submission type discriminator. Omit for services; any value other than "facilitator" is treated as a service submission.

url.description: Base URL of the x402 service. On a free compute host (vercel.app, workers.dev and similar) the endpoint answers HTTP 402 and the submission costs a one-off, non-refundable $1 USDC on Base; on static-only hosting or a dev tunnel it is rejected with HTTP 400 at any price

ServiceUpdateRequest.description: Owner update request body (F10). Send ALL fields prefilled with the live listing values: the server computes the diff and records only what actually changed. Empty or omitted fields are always treated as UNCHANGED (no field can be cleared through this channel; listed endpoints can be removed or change method, with review, through endpoints_remove and endpoints_method). Only declarative metadata is updatable; measured fields (verified, uptime, pricing, status, payTo) are read-only for everyone.

base_url.description: Proposed base URL. Changing it is an identity change and is reviewed with extra scrutiny; the ownership proof is always checked on the CURRENT domain

contact_email.description: Proposed owner contact email; empty string = keep unchanged

email.description: Requester email: receives the review outcome. Subject to the per-(email, service) 7-day cooldown

endpoints_add.description: NEW x402-protected endpoints to add, one per entry, as "/v1/resource" or "POST /v1/resource". GET and POST are the accepted methods (case-insensitive) and an entry with no method prefix is taken as GET. Method and path together identify an endpoint, so "POST /x" is a new addition even when "GET /x" is already listed; an entry already listed with the same method is silently ignored. Listed endpoints are removed or change method through endpoints_remove and endpoints_method. The endpoint is probed for HTTP 402 with the declared method after ownership verification. Also accepted as one newline-separated string.

endpoints_method.description: Method changes of listed endpoints, as "GET /v1/resource -> POST" (current method and path, then the new method) or {path, from, to} objects; GET and POST only, and from must differ from to. The endpoint (from, path) must be currently listed, and the same endpoint cannot be both removed and changed method. After ownership verification the endpoint is probed with the new method, and the change is applied only if it answers with a valid x402 HTTP 402 there. Also accepted as one newline-separated string.

endpoints_remove.description: Currently listed endpoints to remove, as "/v1/resource" or "POST /v1/resource" (no prefix = GET) or {method, path} objects. Every entry must be an endpoint currently monitored on the listing, otherwise HTTP 400. The listing must keep at least one endpoint unless the same request adds one. A removed endpoint stops being monitored after review; its price history is kept. Also accepted as one newline-separated string.

name.description: Proposed service name (the slug NEVER changes: citations and monitor history hang off it)

website_url.description: Proposed website URL (dev-tunnel domains are rejected; free hosting is allowed)

StatusSummary.description: Status bucket counts over the whole services table, plus the listed perimeter. A service is delisted when it has been offline for 30 days or more (its last successful check, or its listing date if it never succeeded, is older than 30 days); delisting is applied when reading and is reversible. total = online + degraded + offline + unknown, and total = listed_total + delisted.

delisted.description: Services delisted for being offline 30 days or more. Counted in total and offline, excluded from listed_total

listed_offline.description: Offline services that are still listed (offline for less than 30 days): offline minus delisted

listed_total.description: Services still listed: total minus delisted, which is online + degraded + listed_offline + unknown

offline.description: All offline services, delisted ones included

offline_30d_plus.description: Offline services with no successful check for 30 days or more (or, if never up, listed more than 30 days ago). The same set as delisted.

services.description: Every service, delisted ones included (listed: false), ordered by name

consecutive_failures.description: Number of consecutive failed checks; 0 when the service is stable. Internal negative monitor sentinels are clamped to 0.

listed.description: false when the service is delisted (offline 30 days or more), the same rule that removes it from the default /services list; true otherwise

uptime_24h.description: Uptime percentage over the latest daily snapshot; null = not yet monitored

SuggestionRequest.description: Paid suggestion body (F11). Only "text" is required; the request must be paid ($0.10 USDC on Base via the x402 handshake). Suggestions are internal and manually reviewed, never published.

email.description: Optional contact email: receives the review outcome

Traction.description: Family 6: measured on-chain traction snapshot for a service, derived deterministically from settler-attributed USDC settlements over the service payTo mapping. null != 0: status "measured" reports real numbers (0 is an honest "never settled on-chain via a facilitator"); "no-payto" (no known payTo) and "unmeasured-network" (payTo only on a network we do not measure) null every metric rather than fake a zero; "unresponsive" suppresses the numbers of a shared-payout member whose probe has been failing for 7 days (settlements on the shared address are not attributed to it while it is down). A conservative undercount. shared_payout marks a payTo shared across services: volume_usd_30d is then attributed PRO-QUOTA (the operator-level figure divided by the current members sharing the payout), a declared convention rather than an individually observed measure, while tx_count_30d and unique_buyers_30d stay WHOLE operator-level integers, never divided or fractional; the ratios top_buyer_share_30d and trend_7d_vs_30d are left whole.

all_time_caveat.description: A-25#2 additive: fixed in-band note that first_settlement_at / volume_usd_all_time / tx_count_all_time are floored at the start of our harvest window (the fixed backfill floor, differing per chain), not the service full history.

caveat.description: Fixed in-band note: the conservative undercount, plus the pro-quota convention when the payout is shared

first_settlement_at.description: TRENO A additive: first observed on-chain settlement over the payTo mapping; null unless measured (never recorded yet). null on a snapshot stored before this field existed.

last_settlement_at.description: Most recent observed settlement across all history; null unless measured

max_settlement_usd_30d.description: TRENO A additive: largest single-settlement amount (USD) over the trailing 30 days. An invariant per-settlement amount, NEVER divided pro-quota. null unless measured, or on a pre-extension snapshot.

measured_networks.description: Canonical CAIP-2 networks that contributed a measurement

median_settlement_usd_30d.description: TRENO A additive: median single-settlement amount (USD) over the trailing 30 days. An invariant per-settlement amount, NEVER divided pro-quota. null unless measured, or on a pre-extension snapshot.

pro_quota_share.description: Cluster fraction 1/(shared_with + 1): the pro-quota slice to apply to the whole-integer counts (tx_count_30d, unique_buyers_30d, tx_count_all_time) for this service nominal portion of a shared payout. 1 on a dedicated (unshared) payout; null unless status is measured.

settled_via.description: TRENO A additive (D1): facilitator ids that settled this service on-chain over the trailing 30 days, ordered by volume. [] when not measured or on a pre-extension snapshot. An invariant fact, never divided.

settled_via_detail.description: A-26#2 additive: settled_via WITH the per-facilitator 30d volume/tx weights, same order as settled_via. [] when not measured or on a pre-extension snapshot. Invariant facts, never divided.

shared_payout.description: A current payTo of this service is also a current payTo of another service; when true only volume_usd_30d is attributed pro-quota, while the counting metrics stay whole operator-level integers

shared_with.description: Count of OTHER services sharing a current payTo (0 when not shared); the pro-quota divisor is shared_with + 1

shared_with_services.description: TRENO A additive (E4): the other listed services currently sharing this payout address (slug + name), for the pro-quota disclosure. [] when the payout is not shared or on a pre-extension snapshot. An invariant fact, never divided.

status.description: Whether the metrics are measured, and if not, why they are null

top_buyer_share_30d.description: 0-1 share of the single largest buyer over 30d (concentration); null when 30d volume is 0 or not measured

trend_7d_vs_30d.description: Ratio of the last-7d daily rate to the 30d daily rate; null when 30d volume is 0 or not measured

tx_count_30d.description: Settlement count over a rolling 30-day window ending when the snapshot was computed (not aligned to UTC days); null unless measured. On a shared payout it stays a WHOLE operator-level integer, never divided (apply pro_quota_share for the nominal per-service slice), so never sum it across services that share a payout.

tx_count_all_time.description: TRENO A additive: settlement count over all recorded history. On a shared payout it stays a WHOLE operator-level integer, never divided or fractional, like tx_count_30d (apply pro_quota_share for the nominal slice; only volume_usd_all_time is pro-quota). null unless measured, or on a pre-extension snapshot.

unique_buyers_30d.description: Distinct buyer addresses over a rolling 30-day window ending when the snapshot was computed (not aligned to UTC days); null unless measured. On a shared payout it stays a WHOLE operator-level integer, never divided or fractional (apply pro_quota_share for the nominal slice), so never sum it across services that share a payout.

volume_usd_30d.description: Settlement volume in USD over a rolling 30-day window ending when the snapshot was computed (not aligned to UTC days); null unless status is measured. On a shared payout it is attributed pro-quota (the address total divided by the services sharing it), so the block sums correctly across services; the daily /volume series stays address-level, do not sum THAT across shared-payout services.

volume_usd_all_time.description: TRENO A additive: settlement volume in USD over all recorded history since listing. Attributed PRO-QUOTA on a shared payout, exactly like volume_usd_30d (all-time over a shared address is still the operator figure divided by the sharing services). null unless measured, or on a pre-extension snapshot.

UptimeDataPoint.description: Daily uptime snapshot for a service

VolumePoint.description: One UTC-day bucket of measured on-chain settlement volume for a service (USDC, settler-attributed; a conservative undercount)

volume_usd.description: Settlement volume in USD observed that day

info.description: Public REST API for x402-list.com - the directory of all services using the x402 protocol (HTTP 402 Payment Required). x402 is an open standard by Coinbase for internet-native, agent-first payments. This API provides programmatic access to service listings, uptime monitoring data, pricing information, and network stats. No authentication required for read access. Rate limited to 200 req/min per IP. Reads are free for agents and point queries; sustained bulk pulling beyond 2,000 GET requests/day per IP (UTC day) on /api/v1/* is metered via x402 at $0.01/request on Base. Metered responses carry an X-Meter-Remaining header (free requests left today for this IP) and an X-Meter-Reset header (the Unix timestamp in seconds at which that daily quota resets, the next 00:00 UTC). The directory data returned by this API is licensed CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); the API specification document itself stays MIT (see license). Reuse is permitted with attribution to x402-list.com. Every 2xx JSON response from the endpoints documented here is wrapped in an envelope carrying a single top-level provenance object (see the Provenance schema) that declares the data license, the required attribution string, and a cite_as canonical URL; those responses also send a Link: <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/>; rel="license" header. To request delisting, email info@x402-list.com or update your listing at /services/<slug>/update. Example values shown throughout this specification are illustrative and synthetic; query the live endpoints for current figures.
info.title: x402 List API

post.description: Runs a FRESH flagship-LLM comparison of an already-assessed shortlist of services for a stated need, and charges x402 only for that fresh reasoning. It never charges to read an already-computed assessment (that stays free on the service detail). The report is a modular envelope: data carries one block per priced module (today the advisor answer under data.answer), and meta carries report_version and the modules_run list, so future modules are additive and never breaking. The paid flow is the standard x402 handshake: the first call (no PAYMENT-SIGNATURE) returns HTTP 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and an accepts[] body (single option, $0.25 USDC on Base); sign the payment and retry the same request with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. On success the 200 carries a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header. You may optionally include a probe target (probe { slug, endpoint_path? }) to also test one listed service live: after the fresh reasoning the server makes a real x402 payment to that endpoint and analyzes the response, and the single accepts[0] amount is then $0.25 plus that endpoint price X. The report then carries a probe_report block with a verdict plus truncated extracts (never the verbatim third-party body). The probe is only offered when live probing is armed, and probe fees are non-refundable regardless of outcome. If the fresh run cannot be produced (an unresolvable shortlist or a model miss) the endpoint answers 503 BEFORE settling, so the caller is never charged. When the payment layer or the on-demand assessment feature is not configured, the endpoint answers 503. There is NO refund. This endpoint is agent-first (JSON only).

example.question: Which of these is the cheapest reliable weather API for a high-volume agent?

post.summary: On-demand paid AI assessment of a service shortlist

get.description: Ranks the directory and returns the best x402 service(s) for a stated need, in one request (no paging). The ranking is the same two-stage relevance-then-quality scoring the MCP x402_find_best_service tool uses, run server-side. It is scored mostly on per-service reliability (live status, verification, uptime, response time), x402 compliance, and price (USD), filtered by category and network, with a SMALL (about 10%) weight on on-chain traction (settlement volume, transaction count, and unique buyers measured per service over its known payTo via recognized settlers, a conservative undercount). A deterministic danger flag removes a service from this surface entirely (its slug is listed in excluded_danger); a residual warning is penalized but kept. When a free-text q is given, each candidate is also scored on how well the query matches its AI-derived capability tags and summary plus its name/description/category (falling back to a plain substring match). The x402 compliance term is the share of deterministic conformance checks the service passes, capped at 0.6 (the floor of the C band) when at least one of its EVM routes is missing the EIP-712 domain parameters a standard x402 client needs in order to sign a payment. That cap is a statement about the payment envelope, not about the merit of the service, and it is what moved the scoring to generation 2. The generation served today is 3, which also gates the on-chain traction term on an absolute 30-day volume floor, discounts a payout concentrated on one buyer, and scores a service that publishes no payTo as zero instead of renormalizing around it. Scores produced under an earlier generation are not comparable with these; meta.ranking_version on every response says which one produced it. This endpoint is free and metered like every other GET on /api/v1/* (beyond the free daily quota it answers 402; see the metering note). Prices are decimal US dollars.

parameters.description: Desired service category from the closed category set (case-insensitive). A value outside the set returns 400; omit for all.

A hard filter on the eligible pool, not a scoring input, so it does not change ranking_version. A value other than true/false returns 400.

parameters.description: Tie-breaking emphasis for the ranking weights. A value outside the enum returns 400.

get.description: Returns the distinct list of categories currently used by listed services. Useful for populating filter dropdowns or submission forms.

Returns change events detected on the live x402 wire: a payTo (settlement address) rotation, a price move, or a schema change (endpoints, networks, assets, or protocol version added or removed). Each event is diffed from the ENTIRE accepts[] a service returns on every probe, so a payTo rotation at an unchanged price - invisible to price-only tracking - shows up here. Newest first, over a rolling window (days). Events are retained perpetually; the window only bounds the feed. meta.type_counts breaks the window down by event type and meta.window_total gives the events in it, so ONE call returns all four figures (before, the breakdown took a filtered call per type plus one more for the total). Both cover the whole window: they are scoped by days and by the service filter, but NOT by the type filter. So with ?type=price_changed, meta.total counts the filtered feed you are paging while meta.type_counts still reports every type; the two are meant to differ. Each type in the enum is always present, 0 included, and type_counts sums to meta.window_total while every event carries one of the enum types; a type not yet in the enum still counts toward window_total but into no bucket.

get.description: Returns x402 facilitators ranked by their independently on-chain-verified USDC settlement volume across all measured chains. Volume is measured directly from blockchain transactions (settler-address attribution, EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization to USDC). It is NOT self-reported or dashboard-quoted. For USDC, USD volume equals token volume 1:1. Each row carries 24h/7d/30d volume + settlement counts, the last on-chain activity timestamp, and the number of settler EOAs. Pass include=timeseries to also receive a per-facilitator daily volume series for charting, and/or include=chains for the per-(network,token) breakdown. Combine them comma-separated: include=timeseries,chains.

get.description: Full detail for one facilitator (TRENO A D5): the list-row volume and settlement figures plus the per-(network, token) chains breakdown (now carrying first_activity_at), the on-chain settler EOAs, per-chain distinct buyers, average USD per settlement, a 7-day-vs-previous-7-day trend, the daily volume series (period=all returns the full history, matching the services), and the listed_services bridge (which directory services settle on-chain via this facilitator). An unknown id is matched case-insensitively and 301-redirected to the canonical id before a 404, since the stored id drives on-chain volume attribution byte-exact. avg_settlement_usd_all and avg_settlement_usd_30d are volume over settlement count and are null (never a fabricated 0) when there is nothing to average; trend_7d_vs_prev_7d is null when the previous window is empty. The buyers total is a declared UPPER BOUND: distinct buyers are counted per chain and never de-duplicated across chains or tokens, so prefer the per-chain figures.

Omit to include both. SEMANTIC CHANGE (treno D3): this filter previously meant "answered a valid x402 challenge and is alive" - that broad signal is now the payment_ready parameter. This tier starts empty and grows only with real payments, so verified=true can legitimately return 0 rows. Applied server-side, so meta.total counts the filtered set. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

Omit to include both. This is the broad discovery signal the verified parameter used to carry before treno D3. Applied server-side, so meta.total counts the filtered set. parameters.description: Filter on the SIGNABILITY of the last observed 402 envelope: true = no EVM route of the service was observed missing the EIP-712 domain parameters (extra.name and extra.version) that a standard x402 client requires in order to sign a payment; false = at least one such route was observed. This describes the payment envelope on the wire, not the merit or reliability of the service. Derived from the eip712_domain_extra check of the latest assessment (the same id that appears in assessment.compliance_failed_checks). A service whose latest assessment has not measured that check yet (never assessed, assessed before the check existed, or assessed with no 402 payload captured at all) matches NEITHER value: omit the parameter to include it. Applied server-side, so meta.total counts the filtered set. Any other value returns 400 Bad Request.

post.description: The ownership token is returned exactly once, by request-update. If it is lost, this endpoint queues a replacement: POST the request_id together with the SAME email that created the request. The new token is delivered BY EMAIL ONLY, to the address already on the request, and never appears in this response. The response is deliberately identical in every case (request found or not, wrong email, already verified, already reviewed, token expired, re-issue already queued): this endpoint is not an oracle for whether a pending update request exists, which is information x402-list does not publish. For the same reason there is no GET. One re-issue per update request: it restores access to the proof, it does not extend the request indefinitely. Lost a second time: send a new update request once the current one lapses, since a pending request with a live token is what holds the 7-day cooldown on that email and listing. A request whose token has already expired holds nothing, so its replacement can go out immediately. Rate limited per IP more tightly than the general API budget.

post.description: Service owners propose changes to the DECLARATIVE metadata of their listing: name, description, website_url, category, contact_email, new endpoints (endpoints_add, each optionally prefixed with its HTTP method), the removal (endpoints_remove) or the method change (endpoints_method) of listed endpoints, and base_url (an identity change, reviewed with extra scrutiny). Measured fields (verified, uptime, pricing, status, payTo) are read-only for everyone and cannot be updated through this channel. All fields are compared server-side against the live listing and only actual changes are recorded; submitting with no effective change returns HTTP 400. The response contains a ONE-TIME ownership token (returned only once, never stored in clear): publish it as a line of a plain-text file at {base_url origin}/.well-known/x402list.txt on the CURRENTLY listed domain, then call verify-ownership. The token expires after 72 hours. After verification the request goes to manual review ALWAYS; the requester is notified by email of the outcome. Nothing about a pending request is public. Cooldown: one update request per (email, service) pair every 7 days (HTTP 429 with Retry-After). Only a live or approved request counts: a rejected request does not, so a corrected one can be sent immediately. A request already verified and under review for the same service blocks new ones (HTTP 409).

get.description: Returns the MEASURED assessment sub-scores over time (x402 compliance grade plus reliability uptime/response windows), oldest first, one point per assessment run. These are the sub-scores only, not the ranked composite score published on the service page (that one is computed live over the current pool by GET /api/v1/best), and nothing on the point is AI-derived; the series is honest-empty until the service has been assessed. Read compliance_passed against the compliance_total of the SAME point, never against the current one: the checklist grew from 11 to 14 checks when the three signability checks landed (x402_version_current, eip712_domain_extra, version_channel_coherent), so the series carries a step at that date. Earlier points keep the denominator they were actually measured with; they are not recomputed, because that would mean rewriting an observation after the fact.

The token is one-shot: on success it is consumed and cannot verify again. If the proposed diff touches base_url or adds endpoints, the standard HTTP 402 probe runs right after verification and its result is attached for the reviewer. Verification never auto-applies anything: review remains manual and the outcome is emailed.

get.description: Returns the MEASURED on-chain settlement volume for a service over time (USD), one point per UTC day, oldest first. Volume is read directly from the chain by settler-address attribution over the service payTo mapping (USDC settlements only), never self-reported. It is a conservative undercount: only settlements the settler-attribution monitor observed are included, so a service can have real volume this series does not yet see. The series is honest-empty until a settlement is observed, and a service whose payTo sits on a network not under measurement will read empty here (see the assessment.traction status for why). Days with no observed settlement are omitted, so the series is sparse (one point per settled UTC day), not a dense daily grid.

post.description: Submit a new x402-compatible service, or an x402 facilitator (settlement operator), to be reviewed and listed in the directory. The optional body field "type" selects the branch: omit it (or use any value other than "facilitator") for a service submission; set "type": "facilitator" for a facilitator submission. Service submissions are automatically probed for valid HTTP 402 responses on the provided endpoints. Facilitator submissions are checked for on-chain presence instead: the enabled EVM chains among the declared networks are scanned for recent USDC settlement activity originated by the submitted settler addresses (30-day window, 15 seconds total budget); Solana and chains outside the measured registry are recorded as declared claims and resolved at manual review. A failed or idle probe never blocks the submission. Every submission of either type is manually reviewed before appearing in the directory. A service URL on a free compute host (vercel.app, workers.dev, pages.dev, netlify.app, onrender.com, railway.app, fly.dev, herokuapp.com, replit.app, glitch.me, deno.dev, pythonanywhere.com, firebaseapp.com, web.app and similar) is answered with HTTP 402: submitting it costs a one-off $1 USDC on Base, non-refundable, which buys a place in the human review queue and nothing more. A service URL on static-only hosting (github.io, gitlab.io, surge.sh) or on a dev-tunnel domain (ngrok, trycloudflare.com, localhost.run, serveo.net and similar) is rejected with HTTP 400 at any price. Website URLs are rejected only when they are dev-tunnel domains. Facilitator submissions are rejected with HTTP 400 for any free-hosting website URL, with no paid option. Each email address may submit once every 7 days per submission type (service and facilitator cooldowns are tracked separately): a second submission of the same type within the cooldown returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header (seconds until the cooldown ends). Submissions still pending after the 7-day review window are automatically rejected and the submitter is notified by email.

post.description: Suggest a change, feature, bug, or data fix for the x402 List directory itself. The feedback channel is paid in x402: every suggestion costs a one-time $0.10 USDC (x402) payment on Base, as anti-spam skin-in-the-game. There is NO refund. Suggestions are internal and manually reviewed; they are never published and there is no public roadmap. This endpoint is agent-first (JSON only). The paid flow is the standard x402 handshake: the first call (no PAYMENT-SIGNATURE) returns HTTP 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and an accepts[] body (single option, $0.10 USDC on Base) plus the app-level error code suggestion_fee_required; sign the payment and retry the same request with a PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. On success the 201 carries a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header. When the payment layer is not configured, the endpoint answers HTTP 503 (suggestions temporarily unavailable).
